Comparison

Elicit vs Consensus

A side-by-side look at Elicit and Consensus, using the details in each tool profile.

Quick take

Choose Elicit when your priority is: systematic reviews and structured evidence extraction at scale. Choose Consensus when your priority is: fast evidence checks on empirical yes/no questions.

Elicit vs Consensus at a glance

CriteriaElicitConsensus
CategoryAI Research ToolsAI Research Tools

Platforms

  • Web

Key features
  • Semantic paper search across ~125M papers
  • automatic data extraction into custom table columns
  • systematic review workflow
  • screening with custom inclusion criteria
  • Elicit Reports
  • PDF upload and extraction
  • Consensus Meter showing agreement/disagreement across studies
  • study snapshots with sample size, methodology and journal quality
  • Pro Analysis
  • Copilot for synthesised answers
  • GPT-4-class summarisation of findings
  • Semantic Scholar corpus of 200M+ papers
Advantages
  • Purpose-built for systematic review rather than generic chat
  • extraction into structured tables is a real time-saver
  • grounded strictly in the paper corpus so hallucination risk is lower
  • transparent about which paper each claim came from.
  • The Consensus Meter is an unusually honest interface - it shows disagreement rather than manufacturing a confident answer
  • very cheap
  • excellent for clinical and nutrition questions
  • strong study-quality signals.
Limitations
  • Corpus skews heavily toward English-language and open-access literature
  • paywalled full texts often unavailable so extraction works from abstracts
  • credit pricing makes large reviews costly
  • extraction accuracy still requires human verification for publication-grade work.
  • Works best on empirical yes/no questions and poorly on open-ended or theoretical topics
  • corpus is English-dominant
  • does not do structured extraction like Elicit
  • the meter can oversimplify a nuanced literature.

Pricing notes

Elicit

Basic free with a monthly credit allowance. Plus around $12/mo billed annually (about $15 monthly) with a larger credit pool and unlimited search. Pro around $49/mo annually for high-volume extraction and reports. Team and Enterprise priced per seat on request. Credits are consumed per paper column extracted.

Consensus

Free tier with unlimited searches but limited AI credits per month. Premium around $8.99/mo billed annually (about $11.99 monthly) for unlimited GPT-4 summaries, Consensus Meter and Copilot. Enterprise/institutional pricing on request. Student discounts available.

Prices change often. Confirm on the official pricing pages: Elicit ↗ · Consensus ↗

Frequently asked questions

What is the main difference between Elicit and Consensus?

Elicit: AI research assistant for systematic literature review. Consensus: Academic search engine that answers yes/no research questions by aggregating findings across peer-reviewed papers and showing a 'Consensus Meter' indicating how much the literature agrees.

When should I choose Elicit over Consensus?

Elicit is listed as best for: systematic reviews and structured evidence extraction at scale. Consensus is listed as best for: fast evidence checks on empirical yes/no questions.

Do Elicit and Consensus have a free plan?

Elicit: Yes. Consensus: Yes. Check each official pricing page, as plans change.
